question: Following a six-day ceasefire, on 1 December 2023 Israel continued its organised campaign of violation of international humanitarian law, primarily in Gaza. The mass attacks on civilians, indiscriminate destruction of civilian infrastructure, forced displacement of civilian populations and mistreatment of prisoners of war point to reasonable a suspicion of war crimes and denial of fundamental human rights by the Israeli army. I would therefore like to know: 1.

Will the Commission, as the EU body responsible for implementing the Treaties, examine the validity of the EU-Israel Association Agreement, which is based on respect for human rights and democratic principles (Article 2), which are now being blatantly violated in Gaza?

Given the escalating violence, including in the West Bank, will the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, Josep Borrell, propose an EU visa ban for residents of illegal Israeli settlements and does he intend to propose to the Council of the European Union a freeze on the assets of Israeli settlers and a ban on any trade between the EU and illegal Israeli settlements?

What steps does the Vice-President / High Representative – or the EU – intend to take towards securing an immediate cessation of hostilities, the establishment of humanitarian corridors, the restoration of the peace process and the elaboration of a peace plan leading to the establishment of a Palestinian state and its international recognition by all Member States of the European Union?
answer: 1. The Foreign Affairs Council had an orientation debate on 18 March 2024 (1) regarding the question of the EU-Israel Association Agreement, which is based on shared values, including the respect for human rights. The Council agreed to continue following this question closely and to invite the Foreign Minister of Israel for a discussion on this matter. 2. Settlements are illegal under international law.

Israel must stop settlement expansion, prevent settler violence and ensure that perpetrators are held accountable. Restrictive measures against extremist settlers in the West Bank are under discussion. Imports from Israeli settlements in the Occupied Territories are excluded from the preferential treatment under the EU-Israel Association Agreement (2).
The EU is not planning to ban settlement products from entering the EU. 3. The EU has committed EUR 125 million in humanitarian aid for 2024.

It urges Israel to improve the delivery of humanitarian aid and to open more access points, and respect the Order issued on 26 January 2024 by the International Court of Justice (3) that ‘Israel shall take immediate and effective measures to enable the provision of urgently needed basic services and humanitarian assistance to address the adverse conditions of life faced by Palestinians in Gaza’.

The EU is ready to support the efforts of the United Nations Senior Humanitarian and Reconstruction Coordinator. The EU is engaging with its partners to revitalise a political horizon. The Commission is ready to contribute to reviving a political process, on the basis of the two-state solution premise.
